_meta.leg: G12 exotica goldens — factor-variable coefficient rows under value labels
_meta.owner: Eval Harness (CONSTITUTION Art 10 — Eval owns tests/eval/**)
_meta.status: ADDITIVE standalone leg — NOT wired into run_eval.py's default gating set.
_meta.oracle: Real StataBE 19.5. Source do-file + full log are committed at tests/eval/golden/g12_factor_valuelabel.{do,log} (authored 2026-07-31, opus-routine-202607311304-97936). Fixture = piet/packaging/sample/fatalities.csv (336 obs), the same bundled sample piet_native's `sysuse fatalities` loads, so oracle and engine see byte-identical data.
_meta.why_no_manifest_cell: This dimension is unreachable from the cobra-facing run_eval manifest: value labels do not survive into hbin (no label field in src/io/columnar.h), so a cobra cell keyed on a labeled factor would compare two identical label-free runs and read GREEN vacuously — precisely the silent-skip class tests/eval/AUTHORING.md exists to prevent. The dimension is PIET-side only, hence a standalone piet_* leg (piet_d1 precedent).
what_is_ASSERTED: A. row-name layer — every coeftable row `name` equals Stata's e(b) column name (`<level>.<varname>`), and is INVARIANT under value labelling. Measured directly: arms A (fully labeled), B (unlabeled) and C (partially labeled) produce identical colname vectors modulo the variable's own name.
B. numeric layer — b/se match the Stata oracle within rtol.
what_is_REPORTED_ONLY: C. label carriage — WHERE the display stub text (`Y83`) is carried in the row object. Stata's own display puts the label text alone in the stub column, under a single `varname` header row; PIET's coeftable JSON is a flat array with no header-row concept and currently has no field for a stub distinct from `name` (row keys are exactly b/ci_hi/ci_lo/name/p/se/t). Choosing the carriage (a new `label`/`stub` field vs a nested structure) is a lane:piet design decision this golden deliberately does NOT prescribe. The runner reports what it finds and never fails on it.

tolerance.rationale: Same policy as piet_d1: the oracle values are Stata's own full-precision e(b)/e(V) readouts (%20.15e), not display-rounded, so a tight rtol is honest here. Base-level rows carry b=se=0 exactly, hence the atol companion.

name_aliases.note: piet_native emits `(intercept)` where Stata's e(b) says `_cons`; that alias predates this leg and is NOT part of the BUG-102 question.

_meta.base_level_note: Stata OMITS the base level from the printed table but keeps it in e(b) as `1982b.year` (b=0, se=0). piet_native omits it from coeftable entirely. This leg therefore asserts over the NON-base rows only; the base-level representation is out of scope and unchanged by BUG-102.

cases.description: Fully labeled 7-level numeric factor. Stata stub column = label text alone (Y83..Y88); e(b) colnames unchanged by the labelling.

CONTROL arm — identical model, no value label attached. Stata stub column = bare level numbers. Pins that the labeled arm's colnames are not an artefact of the fixture: A and B colname vectors are identical modulo varname.

EXOTICA arm — value-label set covers only 1983/1985/1987; 1984/1986/1988 are levels of the factor with no label entry. Stata falls back PER LEVEL, producing a MIXED stub column (Odd83, 1984, Odd85, 1986, Odd87, 1988). An all-or-nothing implementation reads plausible on arms A and B and is only caught here.
